units.function: Embedded-PostgreSQL integration specification for the Secret service: Company/user Secrets, provider configs, versions, bindings/declarations, runtime resolution, access evidence, external import and cross-system failure compensation.
units.dependencyDirection: Application services own Secret metadata and authorization over PostgreSQL, call provider adapters for local encryption/AWS material operations, normalize/synchronize adapter and environment references, resolve values into Agent/routine/system consumers and emit access/activity evidence. Provider-private material remains in version rows while plaintext crosses the service boundary only at create/rotate/resolve calls.
units.keyDataModels: CompanySecret(scope Company|user, managed mode, provider/config, external ref, latest version, owner); CompanySecretVersion(material, hashes, provider version, current/disabled); binding/declaration(target, configPath, required, projection class/allowlist); provider config/default/health; responsible user and credential subject; heartbeat run; access event/outcome/error code; archived cleanup handle.
units.lifecycle: Create reserves local identity then creates/links provider material and activates version; rotate creates or writes a provider version then atomically changes current version; DB failures trigger remote delete/archive compensation and failed compensation persists an archived/disabled reconciliation handle. Binding/declaration sync precedes runtime resolution; Agent API reads require a matching running heartbeat and binding, while generic runtime, responsible-user and ephemeral paths have separate rules. Deletion soft-renames first, removes remote material where available and finally removes local rows; retries tolerate remote not-found.
units.testAssessment: The 79 tests form unusually broad integration specifications for tenant/ref consistency, exact binding/allowlist checks, run-bound Agent access, low-trust denial, per-user ownership, value-free evidence, stable failure codes, unique-index races, managed/external provider lifecycles, sanitized discovery/import, compensation and cleanup retries. The focused command skipped all 79 because embedded PostgreSQL was unavailable, so runtime behavior remains unverified here. Gaps include cross-Company instance bindings, fail-open success-audit writes, Agent/local-implicit ephemeral reads without persisted work grants, disabled-provider deletion that can orphan remote material, and no exact responsibility/data-purpose digest.
units.designRationale: Treat Secret metadata and provider material as a distributed transaction with explicit compensation; let bindings and declarations make credential placement inspectable; distinguish Company-owned and responsible-human-owned credentials; deny long-lived Agent API keys and low-trust contexts; minimize logs/import metadata and retain cleanup handles rather than losing track of remote side effects.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs hybrid-cloud Secret custody and data-export authorization bound to an exact Company, accountable human, Agent, work/responsibility contract, execution node, purpose, version and expiry, with durable evidence that cannot fail open and reconciliation across customer vaults and control-plane metadata.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the distributed compensation state machine, archived/disabled cleanup handles, idempotent provider-not-found deletion, value-free access evidence, stable failure codes, responsible-user credentials, exact binding/declaration allowlists, run-bound Agent JWT reads, inactive/version checks and plaintext-free remote import. Rebuild around Company OS SecretPort plus DataAuthorizationPort: forbid implicit cross-Company authority; require signed grant/action digests and explicit version snapshots; make evidence publication durable before or atomically coupled to release; restrict emergency/ephemeral access to short-lived human-approved grants; perform decryption at an attested customer execution node; reconcile orphaned remote material even when provider configs are disabled.
units.responsibilityConflict: An environment target may hold bindings owned by multiple Companies, making the target itself an authority-sharing channel outside a single accountable Company. Generic runtime and especially ephemeral access are not consistently bound to heartbeat/work/responsibility contracts. Returning plaintext after success-metadata failure means the responsibility record can be absent for an executed access. Local implicit and broad member/Agent authorization do not identify a scoped accountable approver, purpose or data-export contract.
evidence: git history: seventeen commits from 778e775c35834aabe09266fb6d415d3dafbd1deb through 90ead239a81215e673446608e7c7c63a5cc4e525 recorded in the read ledger
2026-08-19 focused Vitest: process exited 0; 1 file and 79 tests skipped because embedded PostgreSQL was unavailable; no runtime pass claimed
units.securityFindings: POSITIVE: long-lived Agent keys, skill-test scope, mismatched/completed runs, missing bindings, low-trust policies, inactive Secrets/versions and foreign provider configs are denied; access records exclude values; provider/raw AWS identifiers are sanitized; remote import avoids plaintext; unique indexes cover races; compensations preserve cleanup handles. CRITICAL tenant-boundary risk: instance-target reference replacement deliberately persists bindings from multiple Companies on one target. CRITICAL evidence gap: resolved plaintext is returned even when success metadata writes fail. CRITICAL bypass risk: ephemeral reads need no persisted binding, and the tested Agent JWT path has no heartbeat run or responsibility grant. HIGH custody gap: server-side provider calls still handle plaintext and no attested local-node sealed delivery is proven. HIGH orphan risk: deleting a Secret attached to a disabled provider config removes DB state without remote cleanup. HIGH authority/integrity gap: no immutable digest binds human approval, exact version, permission/data scope, purpose, work contract and evidence. MEDIUM recovery gap: cleanup handles are retained but no worker/retry SLA, alert or terminal quarantine is asserted here. MEDIUM contract gap: many negative paths still match English messages despite some structured codes.
